method_card.title: How to Use BIDMAS (Order of Operations)
steps: Then Division and Multiplication, left to right.
Then Addition and Subtraction, left to right.
method_card.content:
BIDMAS gives the order to work in: Brackets, Indices, Division and Multiplication, Addition and Subtraction.

Division and multiplication share one level: do them left to right, not multiplication first. Addition and subtraction share the next level, also left to right.

A fraction bar groups its top and bottom like brackets: evaluate each fully, then divide.

problem_bank.bronze_description: Multiply and divide before you add and subtract; work left to right within each pair.
problem_bank.silver_description: Brackets and powers first, then the multiply and divide, then add and subtract, left to right.
problem_bank.gold_description: Multi step calculations with fraction bars, nested brackets and powers, including the power of 0.

bronze.hint: Do the multiplication before the addition.

misconceptions.message: Multiplication comes first: 4 × 3 = 12, then 6 + 12 = 18. Adding 6 + 4 first gives 30, which ignores the order.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: No brackets or powers. Multiplication comes before addition, so clear the × first.

guided_steps.hint: It should match your last line.
guided_steps.done: The × was done before the +, so 18 is right.

bronze.hint: Do the division before the subtraction.

misconceptions.message: Divide first: 8 ÷ 2 = 4, then 20 − 4 = 16. Doing 20 − 8 first gives 6.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Division comes before subtraction, so do the ÷ first.

guided_steps.done: The ÷ was cleared before the −.

bronze.hint: Work out both multiplications, then add.

misconceptions.message: Both multiplications come before the addition: 5 × 3 = 15 and 7 × 2 = 14, then 15 + 14 = 29. Working straight left to right gives 44.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Two multiplications and one addition. Clear BOTH multiplications before adding.

guided_steps.pre: Read it back: the products are 15 and 14, total =
guided_steps.done: Both × were done before the +.

bronze.hint: Do the division and the multiplication, then add.

misconceptions.message: Do 24 ÷ 6 = 4 and 2 × 5 = 10 first, then 4 + 10 = 14. Straight left to right gives 30.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Do the ÷ and the × before the +.

guided_steps.done: Both high priority operations were cleared first.

bronze.hint: Multiply first, then work left to right.

misconceptions.message: Multiply first: 5 × 4 = 20, then 3 + 20 − 2 = 21. Adding 3 + 5 first gives 30.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: One multiplication sits in the middle. Clear it, then work + and − left to right.

guided_steps.done: The × went first, then + and − left to right.

bronze.hint: Divide and multiply have equal priority, so go left to right.

misconceptions.message: Division and multiplication are equal priority, so go left to right: 18 ÷ 2 = 9, then 9 × 3 = 27. Doing 2 × 3 first gives 3.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Division and multiplication have equal priority. Work strictly left to right, so the ÷ comes first here.

guided_steps.done: Left to right, not multiply first.

bronze.hint: Multiply first, then subtract and add left to right.

misconceptions.message: After 5 × 6 = 30, work left to right: 40 − 30 = 10, then + 2 = 12. Adding 30 + 2 first gives 8.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Clear the × first, then work − and + left to right.

guided_steps.done: Left to right stops you subtracting 32 by mistake.

bronze.hint: Clear the multiply and divide left to right, then add.

misconceptions.message: Clear the × and ÷ first: 3 × 8 = 24, 24 ÷ 4 = 6, then 7 + 6 = 13. Adding 7 + 3 first gives 20.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Clear the × and ÷ (left to right) before adding.

guided_steps.hint: Multiply 3 by 8 first, it is leftmost.

guided_steps.done: × and ÷ cleared left to right, then +.

misconceptions.message: Brackets first: 3 + 5 = 8, then 8 × 4 = 32. Skipping the bracket to do 5 × 4 first gives 23.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Brackets first, always.

guided_steps.done: The bracket was done before the ×.

silver.hint: Do the bracket and the power before multiplying and adding.

misconceptions.message: 3² means 3 × 3 = 9, not 3 × 2 = 6. With 9 the answer is 6 × 5 + 9 = 39. Using 6 gives 36.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Do the bracket and the power before the × and +.

guided_steps.done: Bracket and power first, then × then +.

silver.hint: Do the bracket and the power, then multiply and add.

misconceptions.message: 2³ means 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, not 2 × 3 = 6. With 8 the answer is 8 + 16 = 24. Using 6 gives 22.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Bracket and power first, then the × and +.

guided_steps.done: Power and bracket first, then × then +.

silver.hint: Add inside the brackets, then square the whole bracket.

misconceptions.message: (2 + 3)² means 5² = 25, not 2² + 3² = 13. So 50 − 25 = 25. Squaring each number gives 37.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Work the bracket, then square it, before subtracting.

guided_steps.hint: Square the whole bracket, not each number.

guided_steps.done: The bracket was squared as a whole.

silver.hint: Brackets first, then multiply and divide left to right.

misconceptions.message: After the bracket, 3 × 8 = 24, but do not stop there: 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Stopping at 24 misses the final division.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Bracket first, then × and ÷ left to right.

guided_steps.done: Bracket, then left to right.

silver.hint: Brackets first, then divide and multiply left to right.

misconceptions.message: Brackets first: 4 + 6 = 10, then 100 ÷ 10 = 10 and 10 × 3 = 30. Splitting it as 100 ÷ 4 + 6 × 3 gives 43.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Bracket first, then ÷ and × left to right.

guided_steps.done: Divide before multiply because it is on the left.

silver.hint: Do the bracket and the power, then multiply and subtract.

misconceptions.message: 4² means 4 × 4 = 16, not 4 × 2 = 8. With 16 the answer is 16 − 6 = 10. Using 8 gives 2.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Bracket and power first, then × and −.

guided_steps.done: Power and bracket first, then × then −.

gold.hint: The fraction bar groups the top: add it up, then divide by 2².

misconceptions.message: The bottom is 2² = 4, not 2. So (18 + 6) ÷ 4 = 6, then 6 + 15 = 21. Dividing by just 2 gives 12 + 15 = 27.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: The fraction bar groups the top. Work out the whole top, then the bottom, then divide.

guided_steps.hint: Add the fraction and the product.

guided_steps.done: Top and bottom were grouped before dividing.

gold.hint: Clear both brackets and the power before subtracting.

misconceptions.message: (3 + 4)² means 7² = 49, not 3² + 4² = 25. So 49 − 30 = 19. Squaring each number gives −5.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Two brackets, one power, one product. Clear the brackets and the power first.

guided_steps.hint: Subtract the product from the square.

guided_steps.done: Brackets and power cleared first.

gold.hint: Bracket and power first, then each multiply and divide chain, then add.

misconceptions.message: Do not forget the power: (2 + 1)² = 3² = 9, not 3. With 9, 4 × 9 = 36 and 10 + 36 = 46. Using 3 gives 22.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Bracket and power first, then handle each × and ÷ chain, then add.

guided_steps.hint: Start the left chain, leftmost first.

guided_steps.done: Each × ÷ chain done left to right, then +.

gold.hint: Any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1.

misconceptions.message: Any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1, not 0. So 7⁰ = 1 and 1 × 8 = 8, giving 16 − 8 = 8. Treating 7⁰ as 0 gives 16.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Work the bracket, then the powers, then the × and −.

guided_steps.hint: Any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1.

guided_steps.done: 7⁰ = 1 was the trap.

gold.hint: Finish the whole top and the whole bottom, then divide.

misconceptions.message: The fraction bar groups the whole top: (27 + 3) = 30, then ÷ (2 × 5) = 10, giving 3. Dividing only the 3 by 10 gives 27.3.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: The fraction bar groups top and bottom. Build the whole top, then the whole bottom, then divide.

guided_steps.done: Top and bottom each finished before dividing.

steps.label: Identify operations
steps.content: No brackets or indices. Division and multiplication have equal priority: work left to right.

bronze.title: Bronze: multiply and divide before add and subtract
steps: No brackets or powers here. Do all the × and ÷ first, then the + and −.
× and ÷ share one level: when both appear, work left to right. The same goes for + and −.
A common slip is going straight left to right. Always clear the × and ÷ before touching + or −.

steps.label: Check
steps.content: The ÷ was done before the +, so 12 is right.

silver.title: Silver: brackets and powers come first
steps: Now brackets and powers appear. Work out anything inside brackets first.
After brackets and powers, finish with × and ÷, then + and −, left to right.

gold.title: Gold: fraction bars group the top and bottom
steps: A fraction bar acts like brackets: work out the whole top line and the whole bottom line, then divide.
Inside each, follow the usual order: brackets, powers, then × and ÷, then + and −.
Powers of 0 catch people out: any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1.

opener.label: Before any rules
opener.display:
You have a £5 note.
You also buy 3 chocolate bars costing £2 each.

steps.say: You worked out the chocolate (3 × 2 = 6) before adding the £5, without being told to. Written down, the bill is \(5 + 3 \times 2\). Read blindly left to right that would be 5 + 3 = 8, then × 2 = 16, which is wrong. Your instinct to multiply first IS the rule: multiplication before addition. BIDMAS just lists the full running order: Brackets, Indices, Divide and Multiply, Add and Subtract.
No brackets or powers. Do the ÷ and × first, left to right, then the +.

steps.done: ÷ and × cleared left to right before the +. That was the whole point.

steps.say: Now a bracket and a power appear. Both come before the × and −.

steps.done: Bracket and power went first. Gone before any × or −.

steps.say: The fraction bar groups the top. Build the whole top, then divide, then finish.

steps.hint: Divide the top by the bottom, 3.

steps.done: Top of the fraction grouped before dividing. That is the gold move.
